How to season a cast iron pan

Seasoning is polymerised oil, not a coating you buy. Thin layers baked past the smoke point of the oil bond to the iron; thick layers stay sticky and flake off in patches a month later.

Any neutral oil with a high smoke point works. The debates about flaxseed versus grapeseed matter far less than wiping the pan until it looks dry before it goes into the oven.

Rust is not the end of a pan. Steel wool, a rinse, and a fresh seasoning cycle bring back a pan that spent a winter in a damp garage, which is more than can be said for most nonstick surfaces.

Soap is fine. The rule against it outlived the lye based soap it was written for, and a modern detergent removes food without touching polymerised oil.
